one_liner: Header-only C++20 SIMD Philox4x32-10 engine; bulk fill runs 1.3-4.6x std::mt19937 throughput, seekable and reproducible.
what_it_does: A counter-based random engine (Philox4x32-10 from Salmon et al., SC'11) that satisfies std::uniform_random_bit_generator with a 32-bit result_type, so it plugs into std::shuffle and the <random> distributions like std::mt19937. Output depends only on a 64-bit key and a 128-bit counter, so the same seed gives the same bits on any compiler, OS, CPU or thread count, discard(n) jumps in O(1), and state()/set_state() plus a seven-integer text format checkpoint a stream portably. Bulk APIs generate_n/generate fill u32 or float buffers and produce exactly the same sequence as repeated operator() calls.
how_it_is_fast: Philox blocks are independent, so the kernels run many counters in parallel in a structure-of-arrays lane layout: 8 counters per iteration under AVX2, 16 under AVX-512 (native unsigned compare and mask registers for the counter carry) and 8 under NEON as two groups of four; each 32x32->64 multiply is done with _mm*_mul_epu32 on even and odd lanes plus a repack. The kernel is picked once at first use by CPUID/XGETBV runtime dispatch, with [[gnu::target]] attributes so one binary runs on any x86-64. generate_n writes straight into the caller's buffer and skips the 64-word refill buffer that operator() drains, which the project measures as 1.5-2.4x faster than the per-value path.
when_to_use: Parallel Monte Carlo or simulation where each thread or task needs its own independent stream with no locks, and results must not change with thread count.
Jobs that checkpoint and resume, possibly on another machine or standard library, where std::mt19937's library-specific stream format is a problem.
Filling large buffers (a few hundred values per call or more) of u32 or float on x86-64 with AVX2/AVX-512 or on aarch64 with NEON.
Replacing std::mt19937 behind std::shuffle or <random> distributions when you also want O(1) skip-ahead (discard) for stream partitioning.
Cross-checking a CPU simulation against GPU code that uses Philox (the repo documents a seeding mapping to NVIDIA cuRAND).
when_not_to_use: Raw bits per byte with no need for seeking or reproducibility: xoshiro256++ is cheaper per byte on four of the five benchmarked CPUs (vphilox wins only on Skylake-SP).
Hot loops that draw one value at a time on ARM: per-value operator() is 0.87x the speed of std::mt19937 on a Raspberry Pi 5, and the per-value path is 1.5-2.4x slower than generate_n everywhere.
Projects that need a released, packaged dependency: no tag yet (API may still change), no vcpkg/Conan package (open issue #65), single author, 0 stars.
Pre-C++20 toolchains, or GPU kernels (CPU only; no CUDA/HIP backend).
Small bulk calls: an 8-word generate_n costs 1.4-1.9x the raw kernel per byte; the overhead fades only by about 256 words.

integration.dependencies: none at runtime; CMake configure generates vphilox/version.hpp; GoogleTest and Google Benchmark are fetched only for tests/benchmarks
integration.min_toolchain: C++20; CMake 3.24+ for the build/install; CI covers GCC and Clang on Linux, Apple Clang on macOS arm64, and MSVC on Windows
integration.platforms: x86-64 (AVX2 or AVX-512F+DQ selected at runtime, scalar fallback), aarch64 (NEON), any other target via the scalar kernel
integration.thread_safety: An engine object is not thread-safe; give each thread its own engine (distinct key or disjoint counter range). Kernel dispatch is resolved once in a function-local static.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — satisfies std::uniform_random_bit_generator with 32-bit output like std::mt19937 and accepts a seed sequence, but it produces a different stream, a seed sequence fills only the 2-word key, and full speed needs the generate_n bulk API rather than operator()

gotchas: vphilox.hpp includes vphilox/version.hpp, which CMake generates from version.hpp.in, so copying include/ alone without configuring or installing will not compile.

counter() returns where the next refill starts, not the stream position; rebuilding an engine from key() and counter() silently skips up to 64 buffered outputs. Use state()/set_state() or the serialize.hpp stream operators.
Size thread pools by physical cores: the kernel is execution-port-bound, and two workers on hyperthread siblings each lose about a third of their throughput.
The VPHILOX_BACKEND environment variable (scalar/avx2/avx512/neon) is read once per process at first use; next_double() consumes two 32-bit words.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick vphilox over OpenRAND or the benchmark-rngs PhiloxSIMD prototype when you need a CPU-only Philox with runtime-dispatched AVX2/AVX-512/NEON, bit-identical output across backends and a portable checkpoint format; pick OpenRAND if you need the same generator on GPUs, and simdrng or a SIMD xoshiro when raw throughput matters more than seekability.
verified_claims_summary: With the project's Google Benchmark harness (GCC 13.3 on x86, GCC 12.2 on the Pi, CMake Release plus per-kernel ISA flags, pinned to one CPU), bulk generate_n (AVX-512 kernel on the x86 matrix runs, NEON on the Pi) cost 0.22-0.75x the cycles per byte of libstdc++ std::mt19937 on the same machine across a Raspberry Pi 5 (NEON), Sapphire Rapids, Skylake-SP and two Cascade Lake hosts, i.e. 1.3x to 4.6x the throughput; per-value operator() ranged from 0.51x to 1.15x. All numbers are first-party, and cycles/byte is only compared within one machine.
status_note: Actively developed (last commit 2026-08-31), MIT OR Apache-2.0 and header-only so it is easy to vendor, but untagged with a CalVer 2026.08.1 version, 0 stars and one author; the bit stream is declared frozen even though the API may change.
